approach_name: Additive Overlay Fork ("strape/" directory + machine-applied build-time transforms, zero committed diff to upstream files)
overview: strape is a git fork of earendil-works/pi whose branch diff against any upstream tag consists **only of added files** — everything lives under `/strape/` (plus two new files inside existing dirs whose names upstream will never use). Branding, provider restriction and dependency trimming are NOT committed as source edits; they are applied to the working tree at build time by `strape/apply.mjs`, a small idempotent codemod with assert-exactly-once guards, and reverted with `git checkout -- .` afterwards. Consequence: `git merge v0.NN.0` is conflict-free *by construction* (no shared hunks can ever exist), and upstream's own invariants (`npm run check`, committed shrinkwrap, lockfile) stay green on the at-rest tree. A pure wrapper npm package was rejected: `getPackageDir()` (<upstream-clone>/packages/coding-agent/src/config.ts:367-388) resolves APP_NAME/CONFIG_DIR_NAME/assets from the coding-agent package's *own* package.json, so a wrapper cannot rebrand without reproducing the whole asset tree. A patch-queue/rebase fork was rejected because upstream bumps `version` (line 3) next to `piConfig` (lines 6-8) in the same file, guaranteeing trivial-but-recurring conflicts. I empirically validated the three load-bearing claims in the live clone (then reverted; repo is clean): (1) setting `piConfig:{name:"strape",configDir:".strape"}` + `bin:{strape:...}` rebrands the entire CLI — `./pi-test.sh --help` printed "strape - AI coding assistant...", `strape install/update/config...`, and `STRAPE_CODING_AGENT_DIR - Config directory (default: ~/.strape/agent)`, with only **two** residual "pi" strings in the whole help output; (2) moving 5 unused-provider SDKs from `dependencies` to `devDependencies` in packages/ai/package.json shrinks the shipped production closure from **143 to 56 packages** and takes install-script packages from **2 to ZERO**, per upstream's own `scripts/generate-coding-agent-shrinkwrap.mjs`; (3) that trim *requires* also emptying `allowedInstallScriptPackages` in both generator scripts — the generator hard-fails with "allowed install-script package @google/genai@1.52.0 is no longer present" otherwise. I also corrected a research premise: the heavy SDKs are **not** loaded at startup — packages/ai/src/api/*.lazy.ts wrap them in `lazyApi(() => import(...))`, so trimming them is safe and only fails if an Anthropic/Bedrock/Google/Mistral model is actually invoked (exactly the desired behavior).
steps: Set up two repos. Keep <upstream-clone> as the read-only reviewed upstream mirror (`git -C <upstream-clone> fetch --tags` only). Create the working fork: `git clone <upstream-clone> <repo> && cd <repo> && git remote rename origin upstream && git remote add origin git@github.com:<org>/strape.git && git checkout -b main v0.84.0`. All strape commits land on `main`; upstream tags are merged in.

Create the overlay skeleton (all NEW paths, so no upstream file is ever modified at rest): <repo>/strape/{brand.json,apply.mjs,build.mjs,sync.mjs,install.mjs,init.mjs,dev.sh,reviewed-deps.json,RUNBOOK.md}, strape/gates/{reviewed-deps.mjs,deps-diff.mjs,review-diff.mjs,audit.mjs}, strape/settings/global-settings.json, strape/settings/project-settings.json, plus packages/coding-agent/strape-bin.mjs (mode 755) and .github/workflows/strape-ci.yml + strape-drift.yml.

Write strape/brand.json as the single source of truth: {"appName":"strape","configDir":".strape","binName":"strape","packageName":"@exo/strape-coding-agent","keepProviders":["openai","openai-codex","xai"],"trimmedDeps":["@anthropic-ai/sdk","@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime","@google/genai","@mistralai/mistralai","@smithy/node-http-handler"],"contextFilePriority":"agents-first"}.

Write strape/apply.mjs with one helper `replaceOnce(file, needle, replacement)` that throws if the needle count !== 1 (loud early failure on upstream drift) and a `--check` dry-run mode. Transforms: T1 packages/coding-agent/package.json -> set piConfig {name,configDir}, bin {"strape":"strape-bin.mjs"}, name -> @exo/strape-coding-agent, push "strape-bin.mjs" into `files`. T2 packages/coding-agent/src/core/system-prompt.ts:121 -> replace "operating inside pi, a coding agent harness" with "operating inside strape, a coding agent harness", and line ~131 "Pi documentation (read only when the user asks about pi itself" -> "strape documentation (read only when the user asks about strape itself". T3 (cosmetic, optional) packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts -> "Update pi, extensions, or model catalogs" -> "Update strape, extensions, or model catalogs". T4 packages/ai/package.json -> move brand.json.trimmedDeps from dependencies to devDependencies (assert each key exists in dependencies first). T5 scripts/generate-coding-agent-shrinkwrap.mjs:13-16 AND scripts/generate-coding-agent-install-lock.mjs:16-19 -> replace the identical 2-entry `const allowedInstallScriptPackages = new Map([...]);` block with `new Map([])` (REQUIRED: verified the generator hard-fails on a stale allowlist otherwise). T6 packages/ai/src/providers/all.ts -> rewrite the `builtinProviders()` return array (anchor: `export function builtinProviders(): Provider[] {\n\treturn [`) to only `openaiProvider(), openaiCodexProvider(), xaiProvider()`, using KEEP-LIST semantics so any provider upstream adds later is auto-excluded without touching the guard; leave the import lines untouched (no noUnusedLocals in tsconfig, and provider modules only import lazy api wrappers + model-data JSON, verified in packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts). T7 (opt-in via brand.json contextFilePriority="claude-first") packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:71 -> reorder the candidates array to ["AGENTS.override.md","CLAUDE.md","CLAUDE.MD","AGENTS.md","AGENTS.MD"].

Write packages/coding-agent/strape-bin.mjs (the branded bin target, ~12 lines): `#!/usr/bin/env node` + set env defaults only when unset — `process.env.PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK ??= "1"` and `process.env.PI_OFFLINE ??= "1"` (kills the https://pi.dev/api/latest-version check in src/utils/version-check.ts:5,55 and the 4-hourly https://pi.dev catalog fetch in src/core/remote-catalog-provider.ts:6, escape hatch `PI_OFFLINE=0 strape ...`) — then `await import("./dist/cli.js")`.

Vendor the model catalog so builds are offline and catalog changes are reviewable: `npm run hydrate:model-data && git add -f packages/ai/src/providers/data` (the dir is gitignored upstream at .gitignore:11, so committing it is additive and conflict-free; verified packages/ai/scripts/check-model-data.ts only validates manifest well-formedness, with NO max-age rule, so a vendored snapshot never goes 'stale'). This also removes the models.dev/OpenRouter/NVIDIA build-time network fetches from every build.

Write strape/build.mjs (the only build entry point): (1) refuse to run if `git diff --name-only` lists any file outside the transform manifest; (2) `git checkout -- .`; (3) `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`; (4) apply T1-T3/T6/T7 (source+branding only — dep sections untouched so the tree stays npm-ci-consistent); (5) `npm run build:offline`; (6) apply T4/T5 (dep trim happens AFTER install, right before packing — no lockfile regeneration ever needed; empirically verified the shrinkwrap generator computes the closure from package.json graphs + the untouched root lock); (7) `node scripts/generate-coding-agent-shrinkwrap.mjs && node scripts/generate-coding-agent-install-lock.mjs`; (8) assert shrinkwrap has 0 hasInstallScript entries and <= 60 packages; (9) `node scripts/local-release.mjs --skip-bun-install --out .artifacts/strape` (upstream's script already packs tarballs and builds an isolated install whose package.json maps every internal package to `file:` tarballs with matching `overrides`, then runs `npm install --omit=dev --ignore-scripts` — scripts/local-release.mjs:141,248-251); (10) `git checkout -- .` to restore the pristine tree.

Write strape/install.mjs: run build, then symlink ~/.local/bin/strape -> .artifacts/strape/node-install/node_modules/.bin/strape (local-release's own shim at scripts/local-release.mjs:173-185 hardcodes the name `pi`, so create the strape symlink yourself), then seed ~/.strape/agent/settings.json from strape/settings/global-settings.json if absent, and offer `ln -s ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md ~/.strape/agent/CLAUDE.md` for global-memory reuse.

Write strape/settings/global-settings.json: {"defaultProvider":"xai","defaultModel":"grok-4.5","enabledModels":["openai/*","xai/*"],"enableInstallTelemetry":false,"defaultProjectTrust":"ask","skills":["~/.claude/skills"]}. Verify once that the `skills` array is additive to the auto-discovered dirs (packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:812-821 scans <agentDir>/skills and <cwd>/.strape/skills unconditionally) by running `strape config` and confirming both ~/.claude/skills and ~/.strape/agent/skills entries appear.

Write strape/init.mjs for per-project Claude Code skill reuse: writes <repo>/.strape/settings.json = {"skills":["../.claude/skills"]} (paths in project settings resolve relative to .strape/, per docs/settings.md:237) and appends `.strape/` to <repo>/.git/info/exclude so strape never dirties the user's repos. Project-level CLAUDE.md needs nothing — resource-loader.ts:71 already lists it and the ancestor walk (lines 118-156) picks it up.

Write the security gates. strape/gates/reviewed-deps.mjs: read packages/coding-agent/npm-shrinkwrap.json, fail if any package's name@version+integrity is absent from strape/reviewed-deps.json (the human-reviewed allowlist) — this is the literal implementation of 'build only after a proper dependency security review', and it turns every upstream sync into an explicit review of exactly what changed. strape/gates/deps-diff.mjs <oldTag> <newTag>: `git show <tag>:package-lock.json` for both, print added/removed/version-changed packages (same intent as upstream's scripts/check-lockfile-commit.mjs, adapted from staged-commit to tag-range). strape/gates/review-diff.mjs <oldTag> <newTag>: `git diff --stat` plus `git diff -G'fetch\(|spawn|execFile|child_process|apiKey|token|auth|writeFileSync|chmod|jiti'` restricted to packages/coding-agent/src, packages/agent/src, packages/ai/src/api/openai-*, packages/ai/src/api/xai*, packages/ai/src/auth, and scripts/. strape/gates/audit.mjs: `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=moderate`, `npm audit signatures --omit=dev` (requires a real node_modules — a lockfile-only audit silently loses signature/provenance coverage), and `osv-scanner --lockfile=package-lock.json` for the non-CVE-DB coverage npm audit misses.

Perform the one-time initial security review before first use, scoped by the trim: 56 shipped packages (openai, undici, chalk, cross-spawn, glob, minimatch, semver, diff, yaml, typebox, ignore, jiti, highlight.js, proper-lockfile, hosted-git-info, grok-mermaid, @silvia-odwyer/photon-node, @earendil-works/pi-*) rather than 143; read grok-mermaid@0.2.2's source in full (young, single-maintainer, ~1.2k monthly downloads, statically imported by packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/mermaid.ts so it cannot be moved to devDependencies) and either accept-and-watchlist it or vendor it; read proper-lockfile (unmaintained since 2022) and @silvia-odwyer/photon-node (WASM). Code review scope: the bash/edit/write tool implementations, the jiti-based extension loader and package-manager install paths, auth.json storage, and trust-manager — i.e. the four areas that produced upstream's 2026-06-08 CVEs (all fixed by 0.79.0; you start at 0.84.0). Record every reviewed package into strape/reviewed-deps.json; that file is the gate's baseline forever after.

Write .github/workflows/strape-ci.yml (Actions pinned by commit SHA, mirroring upstream's .github/workflows/npm-audit.yml style): `npm ci --ignore-scripts` -> `npm run check` (proves the at-rest tree is still a valid upstream tree) -> `node strape/apply.mjs --check` -> `node strape/build.mjs` -> `node strape/gates/reviewed-deps.mjs` -> `node strape/gates/audit.mjs` -> smoke test `.artifacts/strape/node-install/node_modules/.bin/strape --version && ... --help | grep -q '^strape - '` (catches both a broken --ignore-scripts install and a silently failed rebrand) -> generate CycloneDX SBOM (`npx @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm --omit dev`) into strape/sbom/<version>.json.

Write .github/workflows/strape-drift.yml (daily cron): fetch upstream/main, merge it into a throwaway branch, run `node strape/apply.mjs --check` and `node strape/gates/deps-diff.mjs <lastSyncedTag> upstream/main`. This gives you days-to-weeks of warning that a transform anchor or a dependency is about to change, before you ever adopt a release.

Write strape/dev.sh as a copy of <upstream-clone>/pi-test.sh (tsx straight on packages/coding-agent/src/cli.ts, no build step), trimmed to unset every provider key except OPENAI_API_KEY/XAI_API_KEY under --no-env. Note the dev loop shows 'pi' branding unless you run `node strape/apply.mjs` first; that is deliberate and harmless.
Document the sync runbook in strape/RUNBOOK.md and stop syncing per upstream release (they ship 2-5/week). Sync monthly or on-demand to the newest tag that passes the gates.
pros: Merge conflicts are structurally impossible, not merely unlikely: the at-rest strape branch adds files and modifies none, so `git merge v0.NN.0` can never produce a conflict. This is the single biggest maintainability win over a patch-queue/rebase fork, where upstream's `version` bump on line 3 of packages/coding-agent/package.json sits 3 lines from `piConfig` and would conflict on nearly every release.

The dependency-security win is large, cheap, and measured with upstream's own tooling: shipped production closure 143 -> 56 packages (-61%) and install-script packages 2 -> 0, from a 5-line machine-applied change. That removes the entire @aws-sdk/@smithy tree, @google/genai + protobufjs (+ its postinstall), @anthropic-ai/sdk, @mistralai/mistralai, google-auth-library, jws, ws and long from anything a user installs.

Upstream drift fails loudly and early, never silently: every transform asserts its anchor appears exactly once, `apply.mjs --check` runs in CI, and a daily drift canary merges upstream/main to surface anchor/dependency changes before you adopt a release. When upstream adds an install-script dependency, the emptied allowlist forces you to look at it — the guard failure IS the security review trigger.

Nothing upstream-facing is broken or diverged: `npm run check`, the committed npm-shrinkwrap.json, package-lock.json and biome all remain exactly upstream's on the at-rest tree, so you inherit every upstream invariant for free and never regenerate the lockfile (no risk of transitive versions floating during a re-resolve).

Provider restriction is enforced at three independent layers — dependency absence (hard: the lazy import of @anthropic-ai/sdk et al. cannot resolve), catalog keep-list in builtinProviders() (only openai/openai-codex/xai are ever registered, and new upstream providers are auto-excluded by keep-list semantics), and credentials/enabledModels (soft, UI) — instead of relying on pi.unregisterProvider(), which I verified only removes extension-registered providers and cannot remove a builtin (packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:780-786).

Both Claude Code reuse goals are met with zero code changes on the default path (project CLAUDE.md is already a first-class candidate; ~/.claude/skills via one settings key), with an optional one-line guarded transform available if they want CLAUDE.md to outrank AGENTS.md in directories that have both.

Reuses upstream's existing supply-chain machinery wholesale (.npmrc save-exact + min-release-age, check-pinned-deps, both lock generators, local-release.mjs for registry-free private distribution, --ignore-scripts everywhere) rather than reinventing it, so the strape-specific code is ~500 lines of scripts total.

Builds are fully offline and reproducible after vendoring packages/ai/src/providers/data (no models.dev/OpenRouter/NVIDIA fetch at build time), and model-catalog changes become a reviewable git diff instead of an invisible network dependency.
cons: The build is not `npm run build` — it is `node strape/build.mjs`, and the working tree is transiently dirty during it. Hand-editing upstream files in the strape checkout is disallowed (build.mjs refuses, then reverts), which is a real workflow constraint the team must internalize.

Transforms are string-anchored, so an upstream rewording of the system prompt, a refactor of builtinProviders(), or a change to the install-script allowlist breaks the build until someone updates strape/apply.mjs (minutes, but it is unplanned work and it blocks releases until done).

Trimming the 4 provider SDKs makes Anthropic/Bedrock/Google/Mistral models fail at stream time with a module-resolution error rather than a friendly message; harmless here since T6 also removes them from the catalog, but confusing if someone re-enables a provider without re-adding its dependency.

grok-mermaid (young, single-maintainer, statically imported by the interactive TUI) cannot be trimmed the same cheap way and stays in the shipped 56; it needs a manual read plus a watchlist entry, or vendoring, which is genuine unbudgeted review work.

Renaming the npm package to @exo/strape-coding-agent breaks `strape update self` (it would 404 against the public registry) and disables upstream's first-time-setup wizard via isOfficialDistribution() (packages/coding-agent/src/cli/startup-ui.ts:26-42,115-131). Both are acceptable — updates flow through strape/sync.mjs and the wizard only runs under PI_EXPERIMENTAL=1 — but they are real behavior deltas.

Defaulting PI_OFFLINE=1 also blocks network-based extension installs and tool downloads (packages/coding-agent/src/core/package-manager.ts:44, src/utils/tools-manager.ts:16), so users must know the `PI_OFFLINE=0 strape ...` escape hatch.

Per-project .claude/skills reuse still needs a one-time `strape init` per repo (a 3-line .strape/settings.json plus a trust prompt), because global settings paths resolve relative to ~/.strape/agent and cannot express 'cwd/.claude/skills'.
Vendoring packages/ai/src/providers/data means model pricing/context-window metadata is only as fresh as your last sync (mitigated: refreshing it is one command with a reviewable diff).
effort_estimate: Initial: ~2 engineer-days of build work (repo + overlay scripts ≈ 500 lines: apply.mjs ~180, build.mjs ~90, sync.mjs ~60, install/init ~80, four gates ~150, two CI workflows ~90) plus 2-4 days for the one-time security review that produces strape/reviewed-deps.json (56 shipped packages instead of 143, plus the coding-agent tool/extension/auth hotspot read). Total ~1 week to a trusted first build. Ongoing per adopted upstream release: 15-30 minutes (conflict-free merge, `apply.mjs --check`, deps-diff + hotspot-diff review, build + gates, smoke test), and since you batch to a monthly cadence that is ~30 min/month covering ~10 upstream releases. Add 30-60 minutes on the occasions a transform anchor moves or a new dependency needs review; the daily drift canary means you almost always know about these in advance. Vendored model-data refresh is ~5 minutes per sync.
security_posture: Primary control is a measured reduction of the shipped attack surface: moving @anthropic-ai/sdk, @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime, @google/genai, @mistralai/mistralai and @smithy/node-http-handler from `dependencies` to `devDependencies` in <upstream-clone>/packages/ai/package.json takes the production closure from 143 to 56 packages and install-script packages from 2 to 0 — verified by running upstream's own scripts/generate-coding-agent-shrinkwrap.mjs, which printed "Wrote packages/coding-agent/npm-shrinkwrap.json (56 packages, 10 platform-specific)" with zero hasInstallScript entries. This is safe because the SDKs are lazily imported (packages/ai/src/api/*.lazy.ts wrap them in `lazyApi(() => import(...))`), so nothing loads them at startup and only an actually-invoked Anthropic/Bedrock/Google/Mistral model would need them — and T6 removes those providers from the catalog anyway. Second control is the reviewed-deps gate: strape/gates/reviewed-deps.mjs fails the build if any name@version+sha512 in the generated shrinkwrap is absent from the human-curated strape/reviewed-deps.json, which is the literal enforcement of "build only after a proper dependency security review" and converts every upstream sync into a bounded, explicit diff review. Third, the emptied `allowedInstallScriptPackages` map in both generator scripts means any future upstream dependency with a lifecycle script hard-fails the build until a human reviews it. Fourth, inherited-and-kept upstream controls: exact pins enforced by scripts/check-pinned-deps.mjs, .npmrc save-exact + min-release-age=2, committed package-lock.json (never regenerated by strape), integrity-hashed shrinkwrap shipped in the artifact, and `--ignore-scripts` on every install (empirically fine — esbuild ships prebuilt platform binaries). Fifth, added coverage upstream lacks: osv-scanner on package-lock.json plus `npm audit signatures --omit=dev` against a real install (a lockfile-only audit cannot verify signatures/provenance), and a CycloneDX SBOM per release diffed release-over-release. Sixth, network posture is explicit rather than inherited: strape-bin.mjs defaults PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1 and PI_OFFLINE=1 (no https://pi.dev/api/latest-version, no 4-hourly https://pi.dev/api/models/providers/* catalog fetch), settings default enableInstallTelemetry:false (no https://pi.dev/api/report-install), and the vendored packages/ai/src/providers/data removes models.dev from the build path entirely. Residual, explicitly accepted: no sandbox (upstream's stated design — containerize strape if the threat model needs it); prompt injection via CLAUDE.md/skills content is unmitigated and is amplified by reusing arbitrary pre-existing .claude/skills, so keep defaultProjectTrust:"ask"; the dev-only example workspaces (gondolin/sandbox) still download ssh2/cpu-features/canvas, which never execute under --ignore-scripts and are absent from the 56-package shipped closure — pruning them was rejected because it would force a lockfile regeneration and destroy the additive-only property; and grok-mermaid needs manual review plus a watchlist entry because it cannot be trimmed.
upstream_sync_process: Monthly (or on-demand) runbook, executed in <repo>: (1) `git -C <upstream-clone> fetch --tags` then `git fetch upstream --tags` — the pristine clone doubles as the reviewed internal mirror; (2) pick the newest tag T and review BEFORE merging: `node strape/gates/deps-diff.mjs <lastSyncedTag> T` (added/removed/version-changed packages from the two package-lock.json blobs) and `node strape/gates/review-diff.mjs <lastSyncedTag> T` (stat + grep-filtered diff over packages/coding-agent/src, packages/agent/src, packages/ai/src/api/openai-*, .../xai*, packages/ai/src/auth, scripts/, and CHANGELOG.md for breaking notes); (3) `git merge --no-ff T` — cannot conflict, since strape only adds files; (4) `node strape/apply.mjs --check` to confirm all transform anchors still resolve exactly once (the drift canary usually told you days earlier); (5) `node strape/build.mjs`; (6) `node strape/gates/reviewed-deps.mjs` — any package not in strape/reviewed-deps.json blocks the release until reviewed and appended in its own commit ("review: accept undici 7.x for v0.86.0"); (7) refresh the vendored catalog: `npm run hydrate:model-data && git add -f packages/ai/src/providers/data`, eyeball the JSON diff for openai.json/xai.json; (8) `node strape/gates/audit.mjs`; (9) `node strape/install.mjs` and smoke-test `strape --version`, `strape --help | head -1`, `strape /model` (should list only OpenAI + xAI); (10) tag `strape-v0.86.0-1` and push. Two escalation paths: an `apply.mjs --check` failure means a 5-30 minute anchor update in strape/apply.mjs (the ONLY file that ever needs editing for upstream drift); a reviewed-deps failure means a real dependency review, which is exactly the gate the user asked for. Between syncs, .github/workflows/strape-drift.yml runs daily against upstream/main so anchor breakage and incoming dependency changes are known long before adoption.
rename_verdict: Worth it — and cheap enough that skipping it would be the odd choice. I validated it end-to-end in the live clone: with `piConfig:{name:"strape",configDir:".strape"}` and `bin:{strape:"dist/cli.js"}` in packages/coding-agent/package.json, `./pi-test.sh --help` printed "strape - AI coding assistant with read, bash, edit, write tools", "Usage: strape [options]...", all subcommands as `strape install/remove/update/list/config/auth`, and env vars auto-derived as `STRAPE_CODING_AGENT_DIR - Config directory (default: ~/.strape/agent)` / `STRAPE_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`. Exactly two residual "pi" strings appeared in the entire ~180-line help output: `strape update [source|self|pi]` / "Update pi, extensions, or model catalogs" (one optional guarded string swap in packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts) and the `PI_SHARE_VIEWER_URL` documentation line (leave it; the env var name is literal in config.ts:502-508). Add one more guarded swap in packages/coding-agent/src/core/system-prompt.ts:121 so the model self-identifies as strape rather than pi, and the rename is complete. Scope: bin name `strape`, config dir `.strape`, agent dir `~/.strape/agent`, env prefix `STRAPE_*`, npm package `@exo/strape-coding-agent` (never published; installed from local tarballs via scripts/local-release.mjs). Total cost: ~6 lines of JSON plus 3 string swaps, all machine-applied at build time, so the ongoing maintenance cost is exactly zero merge conflicts. Explicitly NOT renamed: the @earendil-works/pi-* workspace package names and npm scope (~469 files reference them, zero value for an unpublished fork, permanent conflict surface), the PI_* env vars other than the two APP_NAME-derived ones, and CONFIG_DIR_NAME is set to `.strape` and never `.claude` (that would put strape's own settings.json at cwd/.claude/settings.json — the exact path Claude Code owns, with an incompatible schema). Known accepted side effects of the package-name change: `strape update self` no longer works (updates go through strape/sync.mjs, and PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1 suppresses the nag) and isOfficialDistribution() turns false, which only disables a first-run wizard that requires PI_EXPERIMENTAL=1 anyway.
claude_compat_plan: Four pieces, three of which need no code change. (1) Project CLAUDE.md: already works with zero configuration — packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:71 lists CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.MD in the per-directory candidate array and loadProjectContextFiles() (lines 118-156) walks cwd up to the filesystem root loading one context file per directory. Caveat to communicate: within a single directory the first existing candidate wins, so AGENTS.md outranks CLAUDE.md if both exist. If they want the opposite, brand.json's `contextFilePriority:"claude-first"` flips T7 on and reorders that one array — a one-line guarded transform. (2) Global CLAUDE.md: pi only checks <agentDir>/CLAUDE.md, so strape/install.mjs offers `ln -s ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md ~/.strape/agent/CLAUDE.md`. (3) Global skills: strape/settings/global-settings.json ships `"skills": ["~/.claude/skills"]`, the officially documented cross-harness path (packages/coding-agent/docs/skills.md ~lines 43-62; `~` and absolute paths are supported per docs/settings.md:237), additive to the auto-scanned <agentDir>/skills, <cwd>/.strape/skills and the .agents/skills convention. Claude Code SKILL.md files work unmodified — same SKILL.md + name/description frontmatter convention, and pi is deliberately lenient about name-vs-directory mismatches. (4) Per-project .claude/skills: `strape init` writes <repo>/.strape/settings.json = {"skills":["../.claude/skills"]} (project settings paths resolve relative to .strape/) and appends `.strape/` to .git/info/exclude so strape leaves no trace in their repos; the first run triggers one project-trust prompt, which is the intended behavior. Two caveats worth stating up front: the `allowed-tools` frontmatter field is documented as experimental but is NOT enforced anywhere in the code (grep for "allowed-tools" in packages/coding-agent/src returns nothing), so imported Claude Code skills are fully unrestricted; and per upstream's docs/security.md, context files load regardless of project trust, so a reused CLAUDE.md is an unmitigated prompt-injection surface. Reuse skills you wrote, not skills you found.
